text:
Vegas has now won four straight, and this one was decided in a 10-minute burst. Victor Olofsson, drafted 181st overall by the Sabres in 2014, set up the second period with a power-play goal at 3:07 and an assist on each of Ivan Barbashev's two goals, at 4:51 and 8:16. In 5 minutes and 9 seconds, a 1-1 game became 4-1. Olofsson finished with a goal and two assists and was named the game's first star.

The result was fair, though not as lopsided as the score looked. Our numbers give VGK a 68% chance to win if this game were replayed on every shot, and the Golden Knights out-chanced Utah in all three periods. Expected goals, a measure of shot quality, finished 4.69 to 2.25. At even strength, though, the two sides were nearly level at 1.93 to 1.87, so the power play carried the gap. Vegas scored on two of its four chances, including Jack Eichel's snap shot at 2:15 of the first, while Utah went 0 for 1. Mitch Marner picked up three assists, all on Vegas's opening, second-period and late goals. Neither goalie had a good night by our measure: Sebastian Cossa allowed 1.7 goals more than his shots deserved, and Carter Hart 0.75 more.

Utah did not go quietly. Lawson Crouse, Jack McBain and Dmitri Simashev scored, the last on a 6% chance in the third to make it 4-3. Brett Howden's tip-in 72 seconds later restored the two-goal margin, and Utah could not answer again. For Vegas, the winning streak reaches four games. The facts give no streak or record for Utah.
